sources.entry: pygame-ce - An actively developed drop-in replacement with new features and performance improvements (pygame fork).

summary.one_liner: pygame-ce is a community-driven fork of the pygame library for writing multimedia applications such as video games in Python.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a Python library for 2D multimedia development, built on the Simple DirectMedia Layer (SDL) library and several other popular libraries that abstract common tasks. The README names modules for fonts (via SDL_ttf and FreeType), mixer and music playback (SDL_mixer), image loading (SDL_image), and transform.rotozoom and gfxdraw (with embedded SDL_rotozoom and SDL_gfx). It is installed with pip and includes a local documentation viewer via `python -m pygame.docs`, plus an examples directory of small playable programs. It is a fork of upstream pygame, created by former core developers, and aims for more frequent releases and a more democratic governance model. Source builds are supported for contributors or for features still in development.
use_cases: make a 2D video game in Python
build multimedia applications with sound and graphics
learn game programming with example programs
play audio and music in a Python program
draw shapes and sprites on screen
load and display images or fonts in a game
how_to_run: Ensure Python (>= 3.10) and pip are on your PATH
python -m pygame.docs to browse the bundled documentation
For development: build from source with pip install . after installing dependencies
notable: Drop-in replacement for the upstream pygame library, with a community governance model
Documentation available offline via python -m pygame.docs
Includes an examples directory of playable small programs
Embeds SDL_gfx and SDL_rotozoom for drawing and transform functions
caveats: Building from source requires compiling and installing the SDL-related dependencies, which the README describes as the most work
Features in development are only available by building from source
